ROLE: Append a complete CONNACK packet (0x20, Remaining Length 2, acknowledge flags, return code) to a caller-owned output buffer.

SIGNATURE.RAW: int wire_encode_connack(struct byte_buf *out, uint8_t ack_flags, uint8_t return_code)
SIGNATURE.NAME: wire_encode_connack

STRUCT.NAME: struct byte_buf
STRUCT.ROLE: destination for the encoded packet bytes

FUNC.NAME: buffer_reserve
FUNC.ROLE: allocate the whole 4-byte packet before the first byte is written

FUNC.NAME: buffer_append
FUNC.ROLE: append the fixed header byte and the two variable header bytes

VAR.NAME: WIRE_MAX_STRING_LENGTH
VAR.ROLE: unused upper bound constant available to the module

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: buffer_reserve
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 when cap >= len + extra; -1 on overflow or allocation failure
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: the buffer keeps or grows its own storage; no transfer
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1 means nothing was written and the contents are unchanged, so the caller returns -2

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: buffer_append
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: int buffer_append(struct byte_buf *buf, const void *src, size_t len)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 when all len bytes were appended; -1 when nothing was appended
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: no ownership transfer; the byte values are copied
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: cannot fail once buffer_reserve has covered the full packet; a -1 is propagated as -2

LOGIC.INPUT: out: caller-owned buffer receiving exactly 4 bytes. ack_flags: CONNACK acknowledge flags byte. return_code: CONNACK return code.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1) If out is NULL return -1. 2) Validate arguments before writing any byte: if (ack_flags & 0xFE) != 0 return -1 (only bit 0, Session Present, is defined; the other bits are reserved and must be 0); if return_code > 5 return -1 (only 0x00..0x05 are defined MQTT 3.1.1 return codes). 3) If buffer_reserve(out, 4) != 0 return -2 (allocation failure; the buffer contents are unchanged, the caller closes the session and nothing is sent). 4) byte0 = (WIRE_PACKET_CONNACK << 4) | 0x00 = 0x20; byte1 = 0x02 (Remaining Length 2); buffer_append(out, &byte0, 1); buffer_append(out, &byte1, 1); buffer_append(out, &ack_flags, 1); buffer_append(out, &return_code, 1). Because the reserve covered all 4 bytes these appends are guaranteed to succeed; if one still returns -1 the function returns -2 and the caller must discard the whole output buffer rather than put it on the wire. 5) Return 0. The packet is appended after any bytes already queued, so a CONNACK can follow queued output without disturbing it.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: 0 when exactly 4 bytes 0x20 0x02 ack_flags return_code were appended and out->len grew by 4; -1 for a NULL out, a reserved ack_flags bit or an undefined return code (no byte written); -2 when the buffer could not be grown (no complete packet appended). The successful CONNACK for scope R02 is wire_encode_connack(out, 0x00, 0x00) -> 20 02 00 00.
INVARIANTS_USED: the acknowledge flags byte has only bit 0 defined
a queue append never reorders or drops already queued bytes
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: out is NULL or a valid byte_buf owned by the caller.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: on success the last 4 bytes of out are the encoded CONNACK; on -1 nothing changed; on -2 the contents may be unchanged or unusable, and the caller reaches a -2 only by abandoning the buffer.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Not thread safe; the caller owns out exclusively.

WIRE_MAPPING.RULE: 0x20: type 2 in the high nibble, reserved flag bits 0 in the low nibble.
0x02: acknowledge flags plus return code, encoded as the single byte 0x02.
ack_flags verbatim; bit 0 is Session Present and must be 0 for a pure clean-session broker, so this broker passes 0x00.
return_code verbatim (0x00 accepted; 0x01 unacceptable protocol level; 0x02 identifier rejected; codes 3-5 exist but this broker does not use them, and 6-255 are reserved). Fact F023 return codes.

EXPECT.derivation: fixed header 0x20 (type 2 << 4, flags 0) | Remaining Length 0x02 | ack_flags 0x00 | return code 0x00

INPUT.note: scope R02 accepts only Clean Session = 1, so Session Present is always 0

EXPECT.derivation: return code 0x02 = identifier rejected, used for an empty or non-ASCII client id

calls: byte_buf out; buffer_init(&out); force buffer_reserve to fail
